metadata-description: A practical starting point for organizations evaluating Ethereum as open infrastructure for products, operations, and shared systems.
hero-description: A practical starting point for organizations evaluating Ethereum as open infrastructure for products, operations, and shared systems.
intro: Ethereum is public infrastructure that no company owns and no company can switch off. That can give an organization a more open, interoperable, and verifiable foundation for coordination—but it also changes how the organization manages privacy, security, operations, and risk.
questions-description: This hub explains what Ethereum provides, what it does not provide, and how to evaluate whether it fits your organization.
foundation-card-description: Explore open infrastructure, trust boundaries, and the properties that matter for organizational systems.
patterns-card-description: Explore digital assets, market infrastructure, credentials, and shared records.
architecture-card-description: Compare Mainnet, L2s, tailored environments, and a conventional system.
resilience-card-title: How do we protect people and systems?
resilience-card-description: Explore confidential system design, security dependencies, and operational resilience.
foundation-title: A foundation, not a finished product
foundation-description: Ethereum does not provide legal compliance, custody, incident response, or a business model. Public activity is observable unless privacy is designed in. Smart contracts, keys, bridges, providers, and upgrades all introduce risks of their own. Responsible adoption starts with one bounded use case and a clear exit path for users and the organization.
continue-description: Use these guides to move from the architectural question to a scoped, evidence-led evaluation.
